title: The Queue (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist social
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The queue is a social contract entered into voluntarily
At first and then involuntarily because that's how queues be
You join the back and then you wait and then you inch along
And wonder what exactly constitutes the average queue's wrong

[Pre-Chorus]
I joined a queue once that turned out to be two separate queues
That had merged at the front without advising me of the news

[Chorus]
The queue knows something I don't know
It knows that patience isn't virtue — it's the only way to go
The queue is an expression of civilisation's trust
That the person at the front earned it — even if that's not a must
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
There is always a man who tries to edge in at the front
Claiming he only has one item and it's clearly not a stunt
It is actually only one item and the rules say that's allowed
But the energy required to let him through fills the crowd

[Bridge]
The express queue has a limit and that limit is a lie
Twelve items maximum but the definition is held wide
The queue at the airport is the queue of all queues
Where everyone is anxious and nobody chooses whose

[Outro]
Queue knows… we're all waiting in order… queue knows
That's my boy
